title: Exact native multi-Connection and Connection-end clauses

assertions: Four publicly admitted Participants of distinct kinds attach six actual native Connections to one public Session. Two Participants each hold two simultaneous Connections on their own authenticated physical peer.
Each original Connection negotiates distinct physical-peer stream handles and reaches completed admission; the runtime reports six actual slots and four physical readers.

One Participant leaving retires only its Connection. The current public snapshot contains five ready Connections, and Conversation close refuses while these remain. Explicit Session end retires all remaining Connections.
A signed public connection.end carries original cid/sid/connid/operation_id and reason_code1000/reason finished, plus an optional extension retained in its logical intent.
Only that original video Connection terminates; the completed result names the original connection_id and ended=true. Replay returns the same result without another effect.
Actual decoded audio continues on other Connections, and the same physical peer negotiates a replacement video Connection in the same Session.

A foreign authenticated peer cannot end the Connection or create a receipt. A captured termination survives journal failure and late cancellation without resubmitting the effect, and releases current authority while waiting for storage recovery.

profile: Existing actual production Connect listener/public signed native QUIC and bearer HTTP snapshot cases, newly rerun and reconciled to exact assigned clauses. Public create/invite/accept/offer/answer commands establish domain state; provisioning fixtures install credentials and the local media endpoint. No injected Session/Connection rows qualify the positive lifecycle.
implementation: The existing native Connection coordinator already implements these clauses. This report reconciles exact current production behavior; no implementation change is attributed to it.
